To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the DNS should not be a passive entity but should be active and (2) the DNS should use a simple scheduling strategy that does not require detailed server state information.

the DNS can be a very effective load balancer if it is allowed to make decisions based on the domain name and the current load of the server, but it is not useful to make decisions based solely on the current load of a server.
(i) the DNS should not be too active in its load balancing decisions and (ii) the best strategy is to route requests based on the domain of the client, and not based on the server status.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new scheduling strategies for the DNS, which are more effective in balancing the load of a multiserver Web site.
developing and evaluating scheduling strategies for the DNS that will help to achieve better performance in multiserver Web-server systems.
the design of scalable distributed Web-server systems and the analysis of the performance implications of using different scheduling strategies in the DNS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best strategy for a multiserver Web site to use is to use the domain as the only scheduling criterion.
, for multiserver Web sites, a simple, stateless policy, such as the one based on the domain name, can be very effective.
the DNS should not try to do more than just routing requests to the most overloaded Web server.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a more active DNS can improve load balancing and performance, but it is very difficult to achieve a significant improvement in the presence of a highly skewed workload.
a more active DNS, in addition to providing a more accurate address resolution service, can also be used as a simple, but efficient, load balancer.
the DNS can be used to achieve load balancing in a distributed multiserver system, but it should not be used as a centralized scheduler for the whole system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNS should not make its decision based on a static load balancing policy.
a simple, stateless policy can be effective in achieving load balancing and improving performance in distributed Web-server systems.

, in order to achieve good load balancing and avoid server overloading in a distributed multiserver Web-server system, the DNS must use a scheduling strategy that takes into account the domain that originated the client request and the current server state, but not the past history of each server.
